ratings_why.fun: Timing every buy against the Moon and spiking at the Full Moon is a real climb skill, but a pure Hare board pulses rather than grows, and the New Moon fight costs Health every cycle.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7: the Moon's Law turns the genre's core habit, permanent stacking, into shelf-life timing, and the reset itself is spent as gold or lent to other tribes.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken as written; the open questions are numbers for the owner and a sim, so more passes would mostly make it different.

points.text: Dusk-Runner covers Waning and New, but Waning is already a lit fight; covering New and Waxing would put the insurance on the actual dark turns.
Across a whole game a pure Hare board only ratchets through The Moon-Scour's counter; one Tier 4 or 5 piece that grows something lasting each cycle would give climbers a curve, not just a sawtooth.
Charm-Pedlar pays almost nothing at its first New Moons; a small floor on the first one would let it do its Tier 2 economy job on turn 4.
In a pure Hare board Sister Silverpenny just copies another Hare for two fights; letting her keep the copied Full Moon text would give the fallback a reason to exist.

standouts.why: Chalk-Cutter makes seating on the zigzag the skill, and doubling is safe because the light goes out.
Mother Meikle Care turns the reset into lasting power for another tribe, the tribe's best cross-tribe hook.
Jill Longshanks wanting to be brightest pulls against Crescent Sister feeding the dimmest: a real buff-order choice.

weakest.why: Charm-Pedlar is dead early, when Tier 2 economy matters most.
Sister Silverpenny is hard to read and weak in the tribe's own pure build.
March Madcap only reshuffles fight-only light at random; little to plan around.

flags.note: Mother Meikle Care banks half of a multiplied cycle permanently, and the banked amount rises each cycle with the Moon-Scour counter; an Ooze eating a doubled Hare launders the same way.
Golden Dame Waxwell with golden Chalk-Cutters multiplies light about 27 times for two fights; capped by the reset, but a one-fight lobby kill.
Ringside Bookie with Moon-Caller and The Hare in the Moon is a buy, buff, sell gold loop; it looks self-limiting but needs a check with cheap shop buffs.
